note: The words of the Universal World Profile digits, transcribed from the Mongoose Traveller 2e world creation text in assets/2eWorldCreation.txt by Lane D on 2026-11-02 on Johnny's word (question 144, the hex editor plan's question 1). Every entry cites the line or lines it was read from, as `source`, and keeps the text's wording, including its own spellings and ellipses. Words only: the rolls, DMs and conditions these tables sit beside are in rules/mgt2e_data.js. Where the text gives no words for a digit (Tech Level), the section says so and holds what the text does give. Written up in findings/uwp_codes.md.

starport.note: The text: 'Starports are classed from A to E' (1107); the class table gives X at '2 or less' (1116). The Starport Facilities table (1127-1158) gives each class its quality, berthing cost, fuel, facilities and the bases that may be rolled.

size.note: The Size table (269-300): the code, the diameter, an example and the surface gravity in Gs, which 'assume that the world has a density similar to that of Earth' (259-261). 'Worlds of Size 1 or less are asteroids, planetoids, orbital complexes, space stations and other small satellites' (301-303).

atmosphere.note: The Atmosphere table (307-324): composition, an example, the pressure and the survival gear required; an empty pressure or gear is empty in the text. The atmosphere types (348-397) are the text's paragraphs, each given by its first sentence and its lines.

types.name: Tainted
types.words: Tainted atmospheres contain some element harmful to humans, such as an unusually high proportion of carbon dioxide.

types.name: Exotic
types.words: An exotic atmosphere is unbreathable by humans but not otherwise hazardous.

types.name: Insidious
types.words: An insidious atmosphere is like a corrosive one but is so potent that it attacks equipment as well.

types.name: Very Dense
types.words: These worlds have thick N2/O2 atmospheres but their mean surface pressure is too high to support unprotected human life (high pressure nitrogen and oxygen are deadly to humans).

types.name: Low
types.words: The opposite of a Very Dense atmosphere, these massive worlds have thin N2/O2 atmospheres that settle in the lowlands and depressions and are only breathable there – the pressure drops off so rapidly with altitude that the highest topographic points of the surface may be close to vacuum.

types.name: Unusual
types.words: An Unusual atmosphere is a catchall term for an atmosphere that behaves in a strange manner.

hydrographics.note: The Hydrographics table (482-499): the code, the percentage of surface liquid and the description. 'For normal worlds, this will be water; on other worlds with corrosive or exotic atmospheres, it could be a corrosive or exotic liquid like ammonia or methane' (468-471).

government.note: The Government table (543-743): the code, the government type, the description, the examples and the example contraband, each as the text's lines have them; the text's own spellings are kept ('complete for control' at 635).

codes.description: No government structure. In many cases, family bonds predominate.
Ruling functions are assumed by a company managerial elite and most citizenry are company employees or dependants.
codes.examples: Corporate outpost, asteroid mine, feudal domain

codes.description: Ruling functions are reached by the advice and consent of the citizenry directly.
Ruling functions are performed by a restricted minority, with little or no input from the mass of citizenry.
Ruling functions are performed by elected representatives.
Ruling functions are performed by specific individuals for persons who agree to be ruled by them. Relationships are based on the performance of technical activities that are mutually beneficial.
codes.examples: Those with access to advanced technology tend to have higher social status

codes.description: Ruling functions are performed by an imposed leadership answerable to an outside group.
No central authority exists; rival governments complete for control. Law level refers to the government nearest the starport.
Ruling functions are performed by government agencies employing individuals selected for their expertise.
Ruling functions are performed by agencies that have become insulated from the governed citizens.
codes.examples: Entrenched castes of bureaucrats, decaying empire

codes.description: Ruling functions are performed by agencies directed by a single leader who enjoys the overwhelming confidence of the citizens.
A previous charismatic dictator has been replaced by a leader through normal channels.
Ruling functions are performed by a select group of members of an organisation or class that enjoys the overwhelming confidence of the citizenry.
Ruling functions are performed by a religious organisation without regard to the specific individual needs of the citizenry.
codes.examples: Cult, transcendent philosophy, psionic group mind

codes.description: Government by a single religious leader having absolute power over the citizenry.
Government by an all-powerful minority which maintains absolute control through widespread coercion and oppression.

lawLevel.note: The Law Level table (967-1004): the level, the weapons banned and the armour banned; an empty armour cell is empty in the text. The text's last row is '9+', which this file keeps as the level '9+': a digit of 9 or more reads that row. 'A high Law Level indicates that visitors to the world will have their activities curtailed' (921-922).

levels.weaponsBanned: No restrictions – heavy armour and a handy weapon recommended…
Poison gas, explosives, undetectable weapons, WMD
Light assault weapons and submachine guns
All firearms except shotguns & stunners; carrying weapons discouraged

techLevel.note: The text gives no words per Tech Level digit. Its Tech Level table (1249-1267) is the roll's DMs by starport, size, atmosphere, hydrographics, population and government, already in rules/mgt2e_data.js (techLevel.modifiers), and its Tech Level and Environment table (1274-1283) the minimum Tech Level an atmosphere needs (mgt2e_data.js techLevel.environmentalMinimums). What the text does say in words is the communications a Tech Level brings (1238-1247), kept here; the editor shows the Tech Level digit with no words beside it.

communications.words: no telecommunication system whatsoever except for whatever facilities the starport offers
radio and telephone communications between major cities at least but no satellite facilities
a progressively more advanced communications grid
accessible from every point of the surface (communications satellites become cheap and easy to deploy)
